1659-the-girl-with-the-golden-eyes.title: The Girl With The Golden Eyes
1659-the-girl-with-the-golden-eyes.creator: Honore De Balzac
1659-the-girl-with-the-golden-eyes.description: A book by Honore De Balzac. Take the phrase for truth. There all is smoke and fire, everything gleams, crackles, flames, evaporates, dies out, then lights up again, with shooting sparks, and is consumed. In no other country has life ever been more ardent or acute. The social nature, even in fusion, seems to say after each completed work: “Pass on to another!” just as Nature says herself.

arxiv-2112-08112.title: Infrared super-resolution wide-field microscopy using sum-frequency generation
arxiv-2112-08112.creator: Richarda Niemann, Sören Wasserroth, Guanyu Lu, Sandy Gewinner, Marco De Pas, Wieland Schöllkopf, Joshua D. Caldwell, Martin Wolf, Alexander Paarmann
arxiv-2112-08112.description: Abstract Super-resolution microscopy in the visible is an established powerful tool in several disciplines. In the infrared (IR) spectral range, however, no comparable schemes have been demonstrated to date. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate super-resolution microscopy in the IR range ( λ I ​ R ≈ 10 − 12 ​ μ \lambda_{IR}\approx 10-12\,\mu m) using IR-visible sum-frequency generation.

arxiv-2207-02379.title: Some Tradeoffs of Competition in Grant Contests
arxiv-2207-02379.creator: Kyle R. Myers
arxiv-2207-02379.description: Abstract When funding public goods, resources are often allocated via mechanisms that resemble contests, especially in the case of research grants. A common critique of these contests is that they induce “too much” effort from participants. This need not be true if the effort in the contest is itself directed towards the public good.

arxiv-2408-17145.title: Painless Federated Learning: An Interplay of Line-search and Extrapolation
arxiv-2408-17145.creator: Geetika, Somya Tyagi, Bapi Chatterjee
arxiv-2408-17145.description: Abstract The classical line search for learning rate (LR) tuning in the stochastic gradient descent ( Sgd ) algorithm can tame the convergence slowdown due to data-sampling noise. In a federated setting, wherein the client heterogeneity introduces a slowdown to the global convergence, line search can be relevantly adapted.

arxiv-2409-06036.title: Steady-State Statistics of Classical Nonlinear Dynamical Systems from Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum Devices
arxiv-2409-06036.creator: Yash M. Lokare, Dingding Wei, Lucas Chan, Brenda M. Rubenstein, J. B. Marston
arxiv-2409-06036.description: Abstract Classical nonlinear dynamical systems are often characterized by their steady-state probability distribution functions (PDFs). Typically, PDFs are accumulated from numerical simulations that involve solving the underlying dynamical equations of motion using integration techniques. An alternative procedure, direct statistical simulation (DSS), solves for the statistics directly.

arxiv-2506-15935.creator: W. Roland-Batty 1, H. Schunker 1, R.H. Cameron 2, D. Przybylski 2, L. Gizon 2,3 and D.I. Pontin 1 1 The University of Newcastle, University Dr, Callaghan NSW 2308, Australia 2 Max-Planck-Institut für Sonnensystemforschung, 37077 Göttingen, Germany 3 Institut für Astrophysik, Georg-August-Universität
arxiv-2506-15935.description: Abstract Context. Joy’s law describes the tilt of bipolar active regions on the Sun away from an east-west orientation, where the flux of the polarity concentrated at the prograde side tends to be closer to the equator than the polarity on the retrograde side.

arxiv-2508-16842.title: Magnetic Pressure Dominance Stabilizes AGN Disks Against Gravitational Instability
arxiv-2508-16842.creator: Hannalore J. Gerling-Dunsmore, Mitchell C. Begelman, Jacob B. Simon, Philip J. Armitage
arxiv-2508-16842.description: Abstract Magnetic effects have long been considered a possible factor in stabilizing the outer regions of active galactic nuclei (AGN) accretion disks against gravitational instability (GI). However, the computational demands of testing this hypothesis have prevented comprehensive study of this problem.

pmc-10617158.title: Understanding social risk factors of county-level disparities in COVID-19 tests per confirmed case in South Carolina using statewide electronic health records data
pmc-10617158.creator: Fanghui Shi, Jiajia Zhang, Xueying Yang, Xiaowen Sun, Zhenlong Li, Sharon Weissman, Bankole Olatosi, Xiaoming Li
pmc-10617158.description: BackgroundCOVID-19 testing is essential for pandemic control, and insufficient testing in areas with high disease burdens could magnify the risk of poor health outcomes. However, few area-based studies on COVID-19 testing disparities have considered the disease burden (e.g., confirmed cases).

pmc-10626709.title: The development and evaluation of the worker-occupation fit inventory
pmc-10626709.creator: Keyao Lv, Ruican Sun, Xiaofang Chen, Yajia Lan
pmc-10626709.description: BackgroundPerson-environment fit (PEF) theory, one of the foundational theories of occupational stress, has primarily found applications in organizational behavior and human resource management. Given the alignment between the definition of occupational stress and the essence of PEF, we introduced the concept of worker-occupation fit (WOF). To validate our theoretical model, the development of an instrument to measure WOF becomes imperative.

pmc-11411168.title: A Novel Blue Light Laser (445 nm) in Non-surgical Treatment of Chronic Periodontitis: A Clinical and Microbiological Study
pmc-11411168.creator: Indira Mujić Jahić, Mirjana Gojkov Vukelić, Sanja Hadžić, Enes Pašić, Arma Muharemović, Lana Salihefendić, Rijad Konjhodžić
pmc-11411168.description: Objective: This comprehensive research aimed to thoroughly examine the effectiveness of a diode laser (445 nm) in combination with non-surgical treatment in patients with chronic periodontitis (CP) by evaluating a wide range of clinical and microbiological parameters.Materials and methods: Thirty-one subjects diagnosed with CP were included in this study. The total number of treated periodontal pockets was 862.

pmc-11508231.title: Influence of Temperature and Host Plant on the Digestion of Frankliniella intonsa (Trybom) Revealed by Molecular Detection
pmc-11508231.creator: Keqing Yang, Dongyin Han, Jian Wen, Changshou Liang, Canlan Zhan, Yiyangyang You, Yueguan Fu, Lei Li, Zhengpei Ye, Emilio Guerrieri
pmc-11508231.description: Simple SummaryThe effects of temperature and the host plant on the digestion rate of thrips, Frankliniella intonsa (Trybom), were assessed using a molecular diagnostic tool. The digestion rates of F. intonsa were determined as detectability half-lives of plant DNA in the gut content of thrips.

pmc-13043998.title: Machine learning driven LD50 prediction for cancer risk assessment using modern molecular language models
pmc-13043998.creator: Tanuj Sharma, Peter Sona, Jongsun Jung
pmc-13043998.description: IntroductionAccurate assessment of chemical toxicity is fundamental to cancer research, where early identification of hazardous compounds is critical for prioritizing carcinogenicity testing, therapeutic safety evaluation, and regulatory decision-making.MethodsWe developed ChemModernBERT, a ModernBERT-based molecular language model pretrained using a curriculum learning strategy on more than 1.8 million SMILES strings to generate chemically informed sequence representations.
